quizzes.stem: An engineer wants a reminder about a private test server to guide Claude in one repository on their own machine, and never to reach teammates. Where does it go?

options.a: The committed instruction file, under a heading for personal items
options.b: A git-ignored local note beside the root instruction file
options.c: The personal file in the home folder, applying to every project
options.d: The organisation policy file, which only that engineer edits

explanation.b: The local file is personal to one project and is kept out of version control.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a committed file is how a rule reaches the team, as in "the fix is to move the rule into the project file and commit it", so the reminder would reach every teammate.
explanation.c: Ruled out because that file reaches "You, in every project", and the reminder concerns one repository.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that layer reaches "Everyone on the machine, and individual settings cannot exclude it", whatever the project, so it is not a note for one repository.

quizzes.stem: A session starts at the top of a project, and an instruction file sits two levels down in `web/ui/`. When do its lines reach the model?

options.a: At launch, together with the root file
options.b: Only after a restart that begins inside that directory
options.c: When the user runs the memory command
options.d: Once Claude opens something beneath that directory

explanation.d: A file below the starting directory loads on demand.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the files that load first are the ones "above the working directory are loaded at launch", and this one is below it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a lower file loads "on demand when Claude reads files in those directories", with no restart.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the memory command "lists your CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and other memory file locations" and loads nothing.

quizzes.stem: Testing conventions must govern spec files that live in dozens of different folders, and no other file. What delivers that?

options.a: A scoped rule whose glob matches by extension anywhere
options.b: A separate memory file placed in every one of those folders
options.c: An import of the conventions from the project root file
options.d: A section for each project in the personal memory file

explanation.a: One glob follows the type across folders, and the rule loads when a matching file is read or edited.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the guide's reason for the glob is "test files spread throughout a codebase", and a copy in each folder would have to be kept in step.
explanation.c: Ruled out because an import "moves text to another file and loads it at launch", so the conventions would reach every task.
explanation.d: Ruled out because personal rules "apply to every project on your machine", so they neither scope to test files nor reach the team.

quizzes.stem: A rule meant for infrastructure code loads in every session instead. What is the most likely cause?

options.a: Its glob begins with `**/`, which reaches into every folder
options.b: Every rule loads at launch whatever its `paths` entry says
options.c: The YAML in its frontmatter does not parse as written
options.d: The rule's file name does not match the folder it governs

explanation.c: When the frontmatter does not parse, the rule is treated as unscoped.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a leading `**/` only lets the glob match at any depth, while "matching is by file, and the trigger is a Read, Write or Edit of a matching file".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a rule with a `paths` list that parses is scoped: "it loads only when Claude works with a file that matches".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the file name plays no part, since `paths` "is the only field Claude Code reads in a rule".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A project holds `AGENTS.md` for other tools and nothing named `CLAUDE.md`, and Claude follows it. An engineer adds `CLAUDE.local.md` with a sandbox address, and Claude stops following `AGENTS.md`. What explains it?

options.a: The sandbox address contradicts a rule that the team shares
options.b: Local notes load first and replace everything after them
options.c: A local file counts as a memory file that rules out `AGENTS.md`
options.d: Git-ignored files are read in place of the committed ones

explanation.c: The default is that AGENTS.md is read only when no CLAUDE.md file exists in the working directory or above, and the local file counts as one, so the fallback ends.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a conflict matters only for the same behaviour, where "Claude may pick one arbitrarily", and a sandbox address shares no behaviour with the other file, while its presence alone counts: "A `CLAUDE.md`, a `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or a `CLAUDE.local.md` in the working directory or any directory above it counts".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other", so no file replaces the ones after it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a git-ignored file is read beside the committed one and not instead of it: "In each folder the local file comes after the shared one".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A developer moves the sections of a four-hundred-line `CLAUDE.md` into five files in the repository and lists each one in the root file as an `@` path formatted as inline code. After a restart, `/context` shows the root file and none of the five. What explains it?

options.a: Import parsing passes over anything set between backticks
options.b: Imported files wait until Claude reads inside their folder
options.c: Five imports in one file go past the limit on import depth
options.d: Each imported file waits for approval the first time it loads

explanation.a: A path between backticks is a mention and not an import, so the five files were never pulled in.
explanation.b: Ruled out because imported files "are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them", whatever Claude reads later.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the limit applies to chains, since imports can import others "with a maximum depth of four hops", and each of the five is one hop from the root.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the approval dialog is for "Imports that point outside the project", and these files sit inside the repository.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A new rule should apply to every `.ts` and `.tsx` source at any depth under `src/`, and to nothing outside that folder or of another type. Which `paths` entry does it?

explanation.d: The folder prefix keeps the rule inside `src/`, the `**/` reaches any depth below it, and the brace group covers both extensions.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a single `*` stays in one folder, as "`*.md` matches Markdown files in the project root", so only files directly in `src/` would match.
explanation.b: Ruled out because it names one extension, while covering both takes a brace group, as `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` "matches a set, with brace groups expanded".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "`**/*.ts` matches TypeScript files in any directory", so sources outside `src/` would match too.
